text:
maria: Heads up — we need a concise telemetry contract for rollout/canary dashboards. Product wants comparative signals (latency, error, quality delta) + infra inputs (fallbacks, queueing, batch sizes). Can we align on required attrs and sampling?

sam: +1. Main constraints: low overhead, avoid high-cardinality tags, and make it easy to join runtime+infra traces. Proposing two streams: 1) high-frequency numeric metrics (prom/OTLP counters/histograms) 2) sparse detailed events (sampled traces / logs with request payload metadata).

leo: For runtime, mandatory attributes we can emit per request (lightweight): `request_id`, `model`, `model_version`, `route`, `seq_len`, `batch_size`, `latency_ms`, `status_code`, `tokens_out`, `tokens_in`, `quantization` (e.g., `int8`/`fp16`), `cache_hit` (bool). Keep these as low-cardinality strings or enums.

ruth: From infra side add: `instance_type`, `pool_id`, `gpu_util_pct`, `queue_time_ms`, and `fallback_reason` (if any). Fallback_reason should be coarse (e.g., `capacity`, `oom`, `timeout`, `degraded_model`). Don't include customer ids in metrics, use sampled events only.

anas: For the console dashboards we need derived signals: `canary.delta_p95_latency`, `canary.delta_error_rate`, `canary.quality_regression_score`. Also want slice support (by route, model, seq_len_bucket). Suggest we predefine seq_len buckets: `<=64`, `65-256`, `257-1024`, `>1024`.

jay: Telemetry contract idea (OTel attr names):
```
otel.attributes = [
  "redwood.request_id",
  "redwood.model",
  "redwood.model_version",
  "redwood.route",
  "redwood.seq_len_bucket",
  "redwood.batch_size",
  "redwood.latency_ms",
  "redwood.status",
  "redwood.fallback_reason",
  "redwood.instance_type"
]
```
We'll export histograms for latency (p50/p95/p99) and counters for errors/fallbacks.

sam: Important: sampling policy for detailed events/traces: default 1% global, escalate to 100% for canary traffic and for any request that triggers a fallback or a customer-reported alert. We should tag sampled events with `sample_reason` (e.g., `canary`, `fallback`, `manual`, `anomaly`).

maria: UX ask — product wants side-by-side comparison in Console for baseline vs canary with normalization by request mix. Can we compute normalized deltas server-side or do joins in dashboard?

leo: Best is to emit `request_category` (e.g., `chat`, `completion`, `embed`, `rerank`) at ingestion so dashboards can group. Also emit `token_cost_estimate` to help normalize cost regressions. That avoids heavy ad-hoc joins.

ruth: Cardinality note: don't make `route+model_version+customer` a metric tag. Use `route+model_version` for metrics and keep `customer` only on sampled events. High-cardinality alert labels will break TSDB.

anas: For comparative charting, we need these time series for both baseline and canary: request_rate (per-slice), latency_p95, error_rate, fallback_rate, avg_batch_size, cache_hit_rate, and quality_score. Can we standardize series names?

jay: Proposed standardized metric names: `redwood.rollout.request_rate`, `redwood.rollout.latency_ms_p95`, `redwood.rollout.error_rate`, `redwood.rollout.fallback_rate`, `redwood.rollout.avg_batch_size`, `redwood.rollout.cache_hit_ratio`. Quality_score may be separate ingestion from eval pipeline: `redwood.rollout.eval_quality.score`.

sam: Also add metadata for each rollout: `rollout_id`, `variant` (`baseline`/`canary`), `start_ts`, `end_ts`. These are sparse labels for the rollout event stream and attached to sampled events and to a separate rollout metadata endpoint.

maria: Questions for infra: can you guarantee `avg_batch_size` and `queue_time_ms` within 10s precision and export every 30s? Need for SLO charts.

ruth: Yes, we can emit gauge series every 30s. We'll add `redwood.infra.avg_batch_size` and `redwood.infra.queue_time_ms` with 30s scrape.

leo: Implementation detail: runtime will add headroom metric `cold_kv_misses` for cache warming effects. That helps explain transient latency blips during canary ramp.

maria: Alerting thresholds: product wants automated regression detection with signals: p95 latency +20% AND error_rate +50% => block rollout. Can we implement burst-tolerant checks?

jay: We'll implement a comparison query that computes relative change and uses a rolling baseline window (e.g., last 1h baseline vs canary 5m). If delta exceeds threshold with sample count > X, trigger. We'll also add a significance check (bootstrap / min sample count).

sam: Next steps: sam to own telemetry spec doc, leo/ruth to add runtime+infra attrs, jay/anas to build dashboard wireframes. Let's sync tomorrow 10am.

maria: Thanks all — tagging @sam @leo @ruth @anas @jay. deploy-bot: recorded meeting at 2026-03-21 10:00 UTC :calendar:
